account:
Today I have heard several small, possibly connected reports, but I have not established that anything secret or unusual is actually being organized. The neighbour said Townsfolk 02 reported lights or decorations at the bakery. The neighbour had not confirmed this, and said the baker knew of no special occasion. I have not seen the decorations myself.

The neighbour also heard the builder ask for a private meeting with the innkeeper. Later I personally heard the innkeeper invite the builder to the inn for a private supplies discussion. The secretary reported that Freight had been looking for the miller and builder to coordinate warehouse supplies. These could all be ordinary business. The secretary also passed along townsfolk's report that the baker carried a sack of bread near the plaza; I subsequently saw Freight carrying a bread sack near town hall. Bread, grain, supplies, and possible decorations might suggest preparations for a gathering, but that is only a suspicion, not something anyone has confirmed. I do not know whether these reports are connected or whether anything is being deliberately kept from me.

The innkeeper repeatedly requested a meeting tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the great hall to discuss the inn's business. I accepted directly, the secretary recorded it, and the innkeeper said no preparation was needed. That meeting may clarify matters, but I have no evidence that it concerns an event. Separately, the town accounts were not found on the four great hall tables; their whereabouts remain unresolved. The secretary knew of no danger or public damage, no waiting visitors, and no new correspondence. I am now home just after nineteen hundred. Tomorrow I should read my appointment book, keep my scheduled visits, and attend the confirmed innkeeper meeting, while asking calmly for firsthand information rather than treating rumours as facts.
